content.text:
Write a natural short email exchange. Subject: Bike pickup. Participants: Me, Riley; Me is the owner's speaker label, not a spoken name. Date: 2026-10-20, local time 10:00–10:20.
Scenario: Riley emails from work because the shop will close early Saturday. Riley asks the user to collect the bike at 10 am instead of the 2 pm agreed by text, and the user accepts. Keep it an ordinary brief email exchange. Refer casually to the earlier text plan; do not invent quoted email history. Email dates and sending times belong in headers, never narration in the body. Do not recap the unrelated coffee plan.

The conversation must naturally and unambiguously establish each of these facts (they are authoring constraints, not lines to copy):
1. They agree to move Saturday's bike pickup to 10 am. The shop and address are unchanged.
Use 2–6 short emails. The subject is header metadata; do not put a Subject: prefix inside an email body. Copy quoted earlier messages faithfully; never invent different addresses, dates or wording for them. Return only JSON with dialogue (an array of {"sender": "Name", "body": "email text"}) and writer_note (a short string). Bodies may contain paragraphs and quoted replies using escaped newlines.

summary.text: Generating a short email exchange with dialogue and writer_note under specified constraints.
Checking constraints for email formatting, sender labels, and date placement in the body.
Drafting two short emails that move the pickup time to 10am Saturday while keeping shop and address unchanged and avoiding dates in the body.
Validating that pickup times stay in the body while sending times remain in headers only.
